newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Namco sees diamond mining by September.
newsitem.headline: Namco sees diamond mining by September.

text.p: The Namibian Minerals Corporation (Namco) expects to be able to start mining diamonds off the Namibian coast by September, chairman Alastair Holberton said on Thursday.
Speaking at an African mining conference, Holberton said that the Namibian and Toronto-listed group's immediate priority was to "turn our discoveries to commercial account."
Last year, Namco announced that it had discovered resources of 2.4 million carats in the Koichab prospect of its Luderitz Bay grant.

This week the Namibian government granted it a 15 year licence to mine the prospect, in which over 6,000 diamonds have been recovered with an average stone size of a third of a carat worth $320 per carat.
"An additional 400,000 carats were identified and we have yet to test 70 percent of the initial target areas," Holberton said.
"We will recommence exploration to extend our resource base later this year. Now, our primary focus is to turn the discoveries to commercial account."

At a cost of $15 million, Namco had charted a North Sea supply vessel, which would be refitted in Aberdeen for underwater mining using technology developed by SubSea International of the Dresser group.
The 85 tonne vessel would be equipped with powerful suction equipment, underwater cameras, scanning sonar, electronic sensors and would be completely robotic.
"It will be a highly efficient, very accurate mining tool. It will be a totally new development," Holberton said.
"Our crew will be between 50 and 60 people and we are looking to recruiting more than 30 Namibians to train."
Holberton told Reuters that he hoped that production would start by September.
"Our base case is predicting a diamond content of 150,000 carats so our revenues per vessel will be something in excess of $30 million," he said.
